title: You've Got Mail
hint_1: A late-90s romantic comedy built around the thrilling new technology of dial-up internet, back when a modem screech was the sound of romance booting up.
hint_2: A corporate bookstore mogul and a charming independent shop owner trade anonymous emails while he's quietly bulldozing her livelihood, which is the rom-com version of catfishing.
hint_3: You've seen this. A bouquet of sharpened pencils, a chain bookstore swallowing a beloved little shop in the West Village, and an AOL notification that became a national catchphrase.
hint_4: Meg Ryan, Tom Hanks, and the most famous three-word notification of the 1990s — the title is what your inbox said.

title: Young Frankenstein
hint_1: Shot in glorious black and white in 1974, when shooting in black and white was already a punchline, which was sort of the point.
hint_2: A descendant of the famous mad scientist insists his name is pronounced differently, which is the kind of bit a comedy can build an entire castle on, and did.
hint_3: Either you haven't seen this, or you have and that's somehow worse — a hunchback whose hump moves, a horse that whinnies at the sound of a name, and a tap-dancing monster in tails.
hint_4: "Put. Ze candle. Beck." Mel Brooks, Gene Wilder, and a monster in a tuxedo doing Puttin' on the Ritz.

title: Zero Dark Thirty
hint_1: A 2012 film that turned a decade of classified intelligence work into a procedural, and then got Congress mad about which parts were true.
hint_2: The protagonist is a CIA analyst who is correct about everything and liked by no one, which is approximately how the agency wants you to picture them.
hint_3: At this point I have to ask — does "the greatest manhunt in history" narrow it down for you, or do you need the compound, the helicopters, and the SEAL team too?
hint_4: Abbottabad. May 2011. A bearded man on a third floor. You know exactly which manhunt this is.

title: Zootopia
hint_1: A 2016 Disney film that smuggled an allegory about racial profiling past every child in America and most of their parents.
hint_2: A rabbit cop partners with a con-artist fox to solve a missing mammals case, and somewhere in there is the slowest DMV scene ever committed to animation.
hint_3: The fact that you're still guessing tells me something about you. A city of anthropomorphic animals where predators and prey coexist, and the title is just the name of the city.
hint_4: Judy Hopps. Nick Wilde. Sloths at the DMV. The title rhymes with "utopia" because that is in fact what they did.

title: Zootopia 2
hint_1: A 2025 sequel to a film whose entire premise was a one-and-done allegory, which Disney heard and said "do it again, with a snake."
hint_2: The rabbit-and-fox cop duo return, this time chasing a reptile named Gary, which is somehow the most threatening name they could have picked.
hint_3: I want you to think carefully about what you actually know. You're looking at a tagline with three S's in "twissst," which is a hint roughly the size of a billboard.
hint_4: It's the second one. The first one was the name of the city. Add a number. You can do this.
